text: The source coding theorem has two halves. Why does the second one matter as much as the first?
choices: Entropy is not merely a lower bound but is achievable, so H is the exact size of the data rather than an estimate.
Because it establishes that Huffman coding is optimal among all possible codes.
Because it shows the bound applies only to sources with known probabilities.
Because it proves that lossy compression can beat the bound, which lossless cannot.
explanation: A bound alone would tell you what is impossible and nothing about what to build. The achievability half means any file larger than H bits per symbol contains redundancy some encoding could remove — Huffman reaches it exactly when the probabilities are powers of two, and arithmetic coding reaches it in general. The last distractor overstates: Huffman is optimal among *integer-length* codes only.
